newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher, Kia group shares tumble.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher, Kia group shares tumble.

text.p: Active buying interest in core blue chips pushed Seoul stocks to close at a new yearly high of 792.29, brokers said.

But Kia Group shares plummeted as delayed debt payment by a commercial vehicle affiliate caused concerns that the nation's eighth largest group faced financial problems. A group spokesman strongly denied rumours of trouble.
The composite stock index rose 3.24 points to 792.29, off the day's low of 783.32.
"Core blue chips, which are heavily weighted on the index, led the market rise," said Lee Hee-myong of Samsung Securities.
Casey Choe at Union Bank of Switzerland said onshore funds and foreign investors showed strong buying interest in representative industrials.
SK Telecom went limit up, gaining eight percent or 32,000 won to 435,000. Samsung Electronics rose 4,000 won to 73,000 and POSCO added 2,300 won to 62,900.
All six listed Kia Group shares fell sharply after Asia Motors was late paying back 130 billion won in promissory notes due on Monday.

Several merchant banking corporations rolled over notes worth 84 billion won three months for Asia Motors and Kia Motors helped its affiliate to redeem about 300 billion won in debt obligation, officials at financial institutions said.
"We had temporary cash flow problems as other companies are experiencing. But we now have no financial trouble," said Asia Motors spokesman Ahn Suk-woo.
Kia Motors hit its daily lower limit of 14,700 but late buying orders helped the nation's second largest carmaker rebound to close at 15,300 won, down 600 won.
The other five listed Kia affiliates went limit down.

Asia Motors lost 410 won to 4,740, Kia Steel 320 won to 3,680, Kia Service 650 won to 7,570, Kia Precision 640 won to 7,360 and Kisan 900 won to 11,200. Korea First Bank, primary lender of Asia Motors, fell 100 won to 4,110.
Brokers said the rumoured Kia troubles also hurt companies which were thought to be having been financial problems.
Jinro lost 260 won to 7,300, Midopa Department Store shed 350 won to 7,600 and Hanil Synthetic dropped 350 won to 4,700.

"Some investors believed Kia, such a big group, would hardly default on any debts," Choe of Union Bank of Switzerland. "Unless Asia has really serious financial troubles, the negative impact will last for another one or two days at the best."
Brokers said the market need to consolidate to soak up selling pressure looming around the 800 level.
Choi Bum of C.S. First Boston said: "The market was about to consolidate. The Kia issue put a fuse to the downward correction."
He forecast the index would retreat to 720 level.

"The recent consolidation is not as big as expected in low-priced large-capitalised shares, which have benefitted from falling interest rates and the strengthening yen," Choe of Union Bank of Switzerland said.
Lee of Samsung said after a brief consolidation, the market would rise to 850 level on hopes for an economic turnaround.
-- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
